Subject: Quick recap + proposed split-test matrix for cost comparisons

Thanks again for the demo time today — great conversation and appreciate the clarity on your production profile. High-level recap and proposed next steps below.

Top points I took away from the call:
- Production workload: ~2M inference requests/day, median prompt length ~120 tokens, 95th-percentile session length ~900 tokens (KV reuse heavy across sessions).
- Primary success criteria: predictability for per-1M token unit cost and maintaining tail latency <200ms for 95th.
- Hyperscaler incumbent: you’re running an LLM endpoint on HypCloud with autoscaling; billing is a mix of GPU instance-hours + network egress + managed inference margin — you asked for a normalized per-1M tokens comparison.

Proposed split-test / benchmark plan (quick):
1) Small-scale production mirror (3 days each): Redwood hosted vs HypCloud managed endpoint.
2) Test vectors: 50k real production prompts (you to share sample CSV) + synthetic tail cases.
3) Metrics: tokens/1k, per-1M token $ estimate (normalized), 95th latency, batch size distribution, cache hit rate (prefix KV), and error/fallback rate.
4) Config matrix: batching on vs off; KV cache enabled vs disabled; quantized model variant vs fp16.

Attached: a sample split-test matrix and a request for the usage CSV (technova_usage_sample.csv). If this looks good I’ll loop in Kimberly (pricing) and Laura (solutions) to size the hypothesis and give an initial per-1M token delta.

Next steps requested from TechNova:
- Share 50k sample prompts (anonymized)
- Confirm 3-day window preference and preferred dates

Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Great questions — quick answers and an initial normalized TCO approach.

Normalization approach (what we roll into 'per-1M tokens'):
- Runtime compute + GPU kernels amortized across tokens (primary driver).
- Redwood platform margins and autoscaler inefficiency factored in (we report both raw and with margin).
- Exclude cloud vendor-specific egress if you control egress costs separately; include if TechNova is charged by hyperscaler.
- Network and orchestration overhead: we include an average per-request networking cost when it materially impacts token price (we’ll flag it explicitly).

Cache hit measurement:
- We instrument prefix/KV cache hits in the runtime and report hit-rate by token range and by user/session key. For the split-test we’ll surface both token-level hit rate and request-level hit rate (requests that are fully served from cache vs partially).

Latency at larger batch sizes:
- We’ll run experiments with adaptive batching caps. In our prior customers, enabling batching + KV cache reduced per-token $ by ~35% while preserving p95 latency with a small headroom tradeoff (we’ll quantify). For the split test we’ll include a lane with 'latency-first' caps so your SLO is primary.

Initial ballpark per-1M token delta (very rough, based on profile you gave and public hyperscaler pricing):
- TechNova current: ~$42 / 1M tokens (your number)
- Redwood (baseline fp16, no batching, no cache): ~$35 / 1M tokens
- Redwood (batching + KV cache + quantized model): ~$22 — $27 / 1M tokens depending on cache hit rate (50% hit rate moves you toward $22; 20% hit rate closer to $27).

I’m attaching a first-pass worksheet (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-tco.xlsx) with assumptions. Kimberly — could you give a quick sense-check on the arithmetic and whether we should include a separate line for egress? Laura — can you flag any config we should lock for the 'latency-first' lane?

If TechNova can share the 50k sample by Fri we’ll turn the test-around in ~7 business days (including environment setup and run).

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
